outline: This course equips English majors to design and critically evaluate AI-supported language-learning experiences. Using microlearning—short, focused learning experiences organized around a single measurable objective—as a common design framework, students develop the pedagogical, technological, and evaluative competencies needed to use generative AI responsibly and effectively in language education. Throughout the course, students apply principles of AI literacy, microlearning design, learner-centered pedagogy, instructional design, and teacher professional development to create AI-supported learning tools and materials. They gain experience with prompt-based learning activities, educational assistants, chatbots, AI agents, and feedback-oriented applications across platforms such as Mizou, Edcafe AI, Claude Skills, Dify, Coze, and Opal. By comparing and testing these tools, students learn to evaluate their pedagogical value, usability, reliability, adaptability, and appropriateness for specific learning objectives and contexts.

flexible_learning.content:
1. Week 17: Students are required to watch two online instructional videos provided by the instructor. The first video explains how to interpret the evaluation results from the Week 13 evaluation of the six AI tools The second video explains how to use the evaluation results to identify which tools need revision.

2. Week 18: students are required to revise three AI tools from Mizou, Edcafe AI, Claude Skill, Dify, Coze, and Opal and write a revision plan for  these selected tools.
flexible_learning.outcome:
Over the 17-week period, cross-check and record students' viewing hours in the backend of NTUT's i-School PLUS platform, while simultaneously setting up discussion boards on Zuvio to guide interaction.

In Week 18, students submit their revised proposal and tool link via the Zuvio platform.
flexible_learning.assessment_ratio: Learning outcomes from the flexible week(s) account for 10% of the total grade.
